jobs.title: Senior Dynatrace Observability Engineer / Subject Matter Expert (SME)
jobs.description:
Senior Dynatrace Observability Engineer / Subject Matter Expert (SME)

Location:
Remote
Senior Dynatrace Observability Engineer / Subject Matter Expert (SME)
with extensive hands-on experience designing, implementing, configuring, and optimizing enterprise observability solutions using the Dynatrace platform.

The ideal candidate will possess strong expertise in application performance monitoring (APM), infrastructure observability, distributed transaction tracing, automated dependency discovery, digital experience monitoring, and AI-driven root cause analysis.
This individual will be responsible for establishing comprehensive visibility across complex enterprise environments, including applications, infrastructure, databases, integrations, and third-party services. The role requires the ability to correlate performance data across multiple technology layers, identify service dependencies, troubleshoot complex issues, and translate technical findings into actionable operational insights.
The successful candidate will work collaboratively with infrastructure, application, operations, and security teams to enhance observability capabilities, improve incident investigation, and establish proactive performance monitoring practices.
Key Responsibilities

Dynatrace Platform Architecture & Implementation

Design, deploy, configure, and optimize Dynatrace observability solutions across enterprise environments.
Implement and manage Dynatrace OneAgent, ActiveGate, and associated monitoring components.
Establish monitoring strategies for applications, infrastructure, databases, and integrated services.
Configure automatic discovery, monitoring policies, tagging, and logical environment segmentation.
Implement best practices for platform scalability, performance, and operational efficiency.
Evaluate existing monitoring configurations and recommend improvements to increase visibility and effectiveness.

Application Performance Monitoring & Distributed Tracing

Implement end-to-end application performance monitoring across distributed enterprise applications.
Configure distributed tracing to provide visibility into application transactions across multiple services, APIs, databases, and integrations.
Identify application bottlenecks, service latency, transaction failures, and performance degradation.
Establish performance baselines and identify deviations from expected application behavior.
Analyze transaction flows to isolate performance issues and determine contributing components.
Support monitoring of internally developed, commercial off-the-shelf, and web-based applications.

Infrastructure Observability & Dependency Mapping

Configure monitoring for Windows and Linux servers, virtual machines, databases, and supporting infrastructure.
Implement automated application and infrastructure dependency discovery and visualization.
Leverage Dynatrace Smartscape and related capabilities to map relationships between services, processes, hosts, and applications.
Identify upstream and downstream dependencies to support incident impact analysis.
Establish visibility into resource utilization, infrastructure health, and service availability.
Maintain accurate service relationships and dependency information to support operational troubleshooting.

AI-Driven Root Cause Analysis & Incident Investigation

Leverage Dynatrace Davis AI and automated analytics capabilities to identify probable root causes of performance issues and service disruptions.
Correlate application, infrastructure, transaction, and event data to support incident investigation.
Analyze performance anomalies, service degradation, and unexpected system behavior.
Determine relationships between technical events and their impact on dependent systems and services.
Develop actionable problem detection and alerting strategies that reduce noise and accelerate incident resolution.
Support complex troubleshooting efforts involving multiple applications, infrastructure components, and external dependencies.

Business Transaction & Digital Experience Observability

Configure monitoring of critical business transactions and application workflows.
Establish visibility into transaction success rates, failures, response times, and service availability.
Implement Real User Monitoring (RUM) and Synthetic Monitoring where appropriate.
Monitor customer-facing applications and digital services to identify performance and availability issues.
Develop dashboards and reporting that connect application performance with operational and business service outcomes.
Work with stakeholders to identify critical application workflows and define appropriate monitoring requirements.

SaaS & Third-Party Integration Visibility

Evaluate and implement monitoring integrations for supported SaaS applications and third-party services.
Establish visibility into service availability, performance, and integration dependencies where technically supported.
Monitor application interactions with external APIs and services.
Correlate third-party service issues with application and business service performance.
Identify observability limitations and recommend appropriate complementary monitoring approaches.

Change Impact Analysis & Performance Validation

Establish monitoring baselines to evaluate application and infrastructure performance before and after system changes.
Analyze the impact of operating system updates, application upgrades, configuration modifications, and infrastructure changes.
Correlate deployment and change events with performance anomalies and service degradation.
Support performance validation following maintenance activities and technology deployments.
Provide objective operational data to assist with troubleshooting and change-related investigations.

Dashboards, Reporting & Operational Optimization

Design and implement dashboards for infrastructure, application, service, and transaction visibility.
Configure meaningful alerts, thresholds, and anomaly detection policies.
Develop monitoring strategies aligned with service-level indicators (SLIs) and service-level objectives (SLOs).
Utilize Dynatrace Query Language (DQL) and platform analytics to investigate performance issues.
Optimize monitoring configurations to improve data quality, visibility, and operational effectiveness.
Provide recommendations to improve mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR).

Documentation, Collaboration & Knowledge Transfer

Collaborate with application owners, infrastructure engineers, operations teams, and other technical stakeholders.
Participate in technical discovery and requirements-gathering sessions.
Develop platform architecture diagrams, monitoring standards, operational procedures, and configuration documentation.
Provide technical guidance and recommendations regarding observability best practices.
Conduct knowledge transfer sessions for engineering and operations personnel.
Assist in establishing sustainable observability practices and operational processes.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in enterprise monitoring, application performance management, or observability engineering.

3+ years of hands-on experience deploying, configuring, and administering Dynatrace in enterprise environments.

Demonstrated expertise with Dynatrace OneAgent, ActiveGate, Smartscape, and Davis AI.

Strong experience implementing application performance monitoring and distributed transaction tracing.

Experience configuring automated application and infrastructure dependency mapping.

Strong understanding of application architectures, APIs, databases, and distributed systems.

Experience monitoring Windows and Linux infrastructure and virtualized environments.

Proven ability to troubleshoot complex performance issues spanning multiple infrastructure and application layers.

Experience configuring dashboards, alerting, anomaly detection, and performance analytics.

Working knowledge of Dynatrace Query Language (DQL) and modern Dynatrace analytics capabilities.

Experience with digital experience monitoring, including Real User Monitoring and/or Synthetic Monitoring.

Strong analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills.

Ability to independently lead technical investigations and collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Dynatrace Professional certification or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
Experience with Dynatrace Grail and advanced analytics.
Familiarity with business transaction monitoring and service-level observability.
Experience monitoring commercial enterprise applications and third-party integrations.
Experience with SaaS monitoring and API-based observability integrations.
Knowledge of OpenTelemetry and distributed tracing standards.
Experience with AWS, Azure, or other cloud environments.
Familiarity with ITSM integrations such as ServiceNow, Jira, or PagerDuty.
Experience with automation and scripting using Python, PowerShell, or REST APIs.
Understanding of DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), and incident management practices.
Familiarity with change impact analysis and performance validation methodologies.
Understanding of security and network monitoring integrations as complementary sources of operational context.

Desired Outcomes

The successful candidate will contribute to:
Improved end-to-end visibility across enterprise applications and infrastructure.
More effective identification of application and service dependencies.
Faster isolation and investigation of performance issues.
Improved correlation between technical events and business service impact.
Increased visibility into critical application transactions and user experience.
More accurate assessment of performance changes following system modifications.
Reduced reliance on manual troubleshooting and undocumented system knowledge.
Improved operational efficiency through proactive monitoring and intelligent event correlation.
Sustainable observability practices supported by documentation and knowledge transfer.

jobs.title: Senior Civil Engineer SME - AI Data Centers
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

This job opportunity is available at ANY location in the United States. Ideally, selected candidates will be near a JACOBS U.S. based office, but we intend to hire the "best" candidates.

Your Impact

Jacobs' Data Center & Hyperscale practice is experiencing record growth — and civil engineering is at the center of it. From the $10B+ Hut 8 River Bend campus in Louisiana to our strategic NVIDIA partnership driving next-generation AI factory development, Jacobs is delivering some of the most technically complex hyperscale programs in North America. We are building the practice's civil engineering leadership bench to match that ambition.

As a Senior Civil Engineer SME within our Advanced Manufacturing group, you will serve as the technical authority for civil site engineering across a national portfolio of hyperscale data center and advanced technology campus programs. This is not a project-only role — you are setting the civil engineering standards, governing the quality of civil deliverables produced by project teams and Global Integrated Delivery (GID) partners, mentoring the next generation of Jacobs civil engineers, and leading the permitting and regulatory strategy on programs that have no tolerance for schedule risk.

This role is open to candidates located anywhere near a Jacobs US office. Jacobs will recruit the best available civil SME — geography is a filter, not a barrier.

What You'll Do

Civil Site Design & Technical Leadership

You will lead civil site engineering across the full design lifecycle for multi-building hyperscale campus programs — from site selection and feasibility through construction documents, permit applications, and construction administration

Lead campus-scale mass grading and earthwork design for hyperscale programs of 50–1,000+ acres, including cut and fill optimization, soil import and export strategy, phased grading sequencing that maintains continuous operation of in-service facility phases, subgrade preparation specifications, and earthwork volume tracking.
Design and govern stormwater management infrastructure for large impervious-surface campuses storm sewer collection and hydraulic analysis, wet ponds, bioretention, underground detention, and discharge management consistent with post-development hydrology constraints and NPDES permit conditions.
Lead site utility infrastructure design for hyperscale campuses — domestic water service, sanitary sewer capacity and routing, natural gas for emergency generator systems, fire protection water supply, and cooling tower makeup water, including reclaimed water systems to support Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) targets.
Design heavy-duty pavement systems for campus roads, diesel fuel delivery routes, cooling tower crane access pads, transformer pad access, and security perimeters — accounting for extreme axle loads and repetitive heavy vehicle cycles unique to mission-critical facility operations.
Provide civil technical leadership for underground fuel storage systems (UST) supporting large generator plants secondary containment design, leak detection integration, spill containment grading, and EPA and state UST regulatory compliance.
Coordinate geotechnical investigation programs with subconsultants; interpret boring logs and laboratory test data; translate geotechnical findings into earthwork specifications, compaction criteria, and foundation coordination inputs for the structural engineering team.
Develop and maintain Jacobs civil engineering design standards, grading and drainage specification templates, standard detail libraries, and stormwater BMP criteria for the data center practice — ensuring consistency and quality across a national project portfolio.
Provide technical governance for civil deliverables produced by project teams and GID partners reviewing grading plans, utility plans, drainage reports, SWPPP documents, and IFC construction drawings for code compliance, permit condition adherence, and Jacobs quality standards.
Mentor mid-level and junior civil engineers across the practice — developing technical depth, standards fluency, and project leadership capability.

Permitting, Entitlements & Regulatory Strategy

Hyperscale data center programs require complex, multi-agency permitting and land development entitlements that directly constrain site feasibility and construction schedule. The civil SME owns the regulatory pathway

Lead land use entitlement strategy for greenfield and adaptive-reuse hyperscale campus sites — rezoning applications, conditional use permits, site plan approvals, and variance requests — working closely with owners, land use counsel, and local planning authorities to protect schedule and maximize development yield.
Direct NPDES Construction General Permit compliance strategy for large disturbed-area programs, including SWPPP development, BMP selection, QSP coordination, inspection program design, and regulatory agency response. Navigate state-specific regimes including Virginia VSMP, AZPDES, Texas CGP, and similar frameworks with schedule-sensitive permit sequencing strategies.
Lead Clean Water Act Section 404 and Section 401 permitting for sites with jurisdictional wetlands, waterways, or Waters of the U.S. — including wetland delineation coordination, permit application strategy, mitigation planning, and agency negotiation to protect program schedule.
Navigate floodplain permitting, LOMR/CLOMR applications, and endangered species Section 7 consultations for complex hyperscale site development programs in regulated markets.
Develop early-release civil permit packages — rough grading permits, land disturbance permits, and utility installation permits — sequenced to support fast-track Design-Build and EPCM construction schedules while full entitlement packages are advanced in parallel.
Serve as the civil SME interface with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ), state regulatory agencies, utility providers, and local planning bodies throughout design, permitting, and construction administration phases.

Here's what you'll need

Required Background

Successful candidates will possess direct experience managing the planning, design, engineering, construction, commissioning, or expansion of AI, Hyperscale, or Colocation commercial and government data center facilities. Candidates with experience supporting other mission-critical environments, such as semiconductor fabrication facilities, advanced manufacturing, pharmaceutical, or heavy industrial projects with complex electrical and mechanical infrastructure, may also be considered. Experience limited to transportation, commercial, light industrial, government (municipal, state or Federal) institutional, or conventional building projects may not provide the specialized expertise required for this role. Preference will be given to candidates with demonstrated success delivering AI, Hyperscale, or Colocation data center projects.

Technical Qualifications

Civil PE License Active Professional Engineer (Civil) license in at least one US state; NCEES Record maintained; willingness to obtain reciprocal licensure in additional states as project needs require. PE sign-off authority is required at SME level — this is a hard requirement.
Experience 15 or more years of civil engineering experience, including 8 or more years leading site civil design for large-site industrial, technology campus, or mission-critical facility programs. Candidates with strong adjacent-sector depth (pharmaceutical campus, power facility, military installation) who can demonstrate the transferability of their large-site civil skills are encouraged to apply.
Civil 3D Expert proficiency in AutoCAD Civil 3D — corridor modeling, grading surfaces, pipe network design, and plan/profile sheet production for large campus programs. Civil 3D is the production standard for Jacobs data center civil work.
Stormwater & Drainage Deep working knowledge of stormwater management design including SWPPP development, post-construction BMP design (ponds, bioretention, underground detention), and hydraulic modeling. Experience navigating NPDES permitting and state-level land disturbance regulatory programs.
Multi-Discipline Collaboration Demonstrated experience coordinating civil site scope with structural, MEP, and electrical disciplines — including utility routing conflict resolution, foundation clearance coordination, and underground ductbank integration in a multi-discipline delivery environment.
Education Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering from an accredited institution.
Communication Strong written and verbal communication skills; demonstrated ability to present to clients, AHJs, and multi-discipline project teams and to represent the civil engineering scope in pursuit presentations and proposal development.

Ideally, You'll Also Have

Master of Science in Engineering
Experience with Virginia VSMP, AZPDES, Texas Construction General Permit, or other complex multi-agency regulatory frameworks for large land disturbance programs.
Design-Build or EPCM delivery experience — having served as civil engineer of record or civil lead on a DB or EPCM contract, with experience developing early-release grading permit packages and integrating with GC-led construction teams.
Direct experience on hyperscale or colocation data center campus programs at 50+ acres, including pad elevation strategy, phased grading, and campus-scale utility systems.
CFM (Certified Floodplain Manager), ENV SP (Environmental Professional), QISP or QSP designation supporting stormwater compliance program leadership.
LEED AP or sustainability-related credential; familiarity with how site civil design contributes to LEED BD+C certification for large campus programs.
Experience with Section 404/401 and USACE permitting for jurisdictional wetlands or Waters of the U.S. on large development programs.
Navisworks multi-discipline model coordination experience for underground utility conflict resolution.
Bluebeam Revu proficiency for document review and markup workflows.
Industry visibility through technical publications, ASCE presentations, or client-facing thought leadership in the data center or advanced technology market.

Jacobs offers a competitive base salary range of $169,000 – $233,000 depending on experience and qualifications, plus a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, and professional development support including PE reciprocity sponsorship and continuing education funding. Jacobs is committed to growing diverse engineering leadership at the SME level.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $169,500.00 to $233,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

SENIOR CIVIL ENGINEER / PROJECT MANAGER -

PROFESSIONAL ENGINEER

Project Control Engineering, LLC

Algonac, Michigan | Flexible Hybrid Arrangement

Performance Bonus + Sign-On/Relocation Support

Our client is seeking an experienced Professional Engineer to join our civil engineering team as a Senior Civil Engineer/Project Manager.

This is an opportunity for a capable engineer to assume meaningful responsibility for projects, clients, technical decisions, and the development of other professionals. The successful candidate will work directly with PCE’s ownership, project managers, engineers, survey personnel, technicians, and field staff to deliver municipal infrastructure and private-development projects throughout Southeast Michigan.

This is not a narrowly defined production position. The selected engineer will have the opportunity to manage projects from initial scope through design and construction, participate in important client decisions, mentor experienced staff, improve project-delivery practices, and exercise professional judgment over work performed under their responsible charge.

Our services include:

Municipal engineering
Water distribution and treatment-related infrastructure
Sanitary sewer collection and rehabilitation
Stormwater management and drainage
Roadway and streetscape improvements
Private land development and site design
Utility planning and coordination
Professional surveying
Construction administration and observation
CCTV and infrastructure investigation
Grant-supported public infrastructure projects

PCE has built its reputation through long-term relationships, local knowledge, practical engineering, responsiveness, and personal accountability to our clients.

The Opportunity

The Senior Civil Engineer / Project Manager will lead and support civil engineering projects from initial planning through final design, permitting, bidding, construction, and closeout.

Depending on experience and demonstrated capabilities, the successful candidate will:

Exercise responsible charge over engineering work within their areas of competence.
Manage municipal and private-development projects.
Review and approve plans, calculations, specifications, reports, and technical documents.
Lead project teams consisting of engineers, designers, survey personnel, technicians, subconsultants, and construction staff.
Develop direct working relationships with municipal officials, developers, contractors, review agencies, and other clients.
Mentor technical staff and help strengthen PCE’s engineering standards.
Participate in proposals, interviews, fee development, and business-development activities.
Influence how projects and the engineering practice are managed.

This position provides a strong advancement opportunity for an engineer who wants more responsibility, greater client exposure, and a clearer voice in the direction of a professional practice.

Primary Responsibilities

Engineering Design and Technical Leadership

Lead and perform civil engineering analysis and design for municipal infrastructure and private-development projects.
Prepare and review engineering plans, calculations, specifications, cost estimates, reports, permit applications, and bidding documents.
Provide technical direction to engineers, designers, technicians, survey staff, and other project participants.
Review grading, drainage, stormwater, water-main, sanitary-sewer, roadway, utility, site-layout, and related civil engineering designs.
Confirm that designs comply with applicable codes, standards, permit requirements, client expectations, and accepted engineering practice.
Identify technical risks, incomplete information, conflicts, and constructability concerns early in the design process.
Exercise responsible charge over assigned work and sign and seal documents only within the engineer’s areas of competence and professional control.
Support development and continuous improvement of PCE’s engineering standards, details, specifications, calculations, and QA/QC procedures.

Project Management

Manage projects from authorization through final completion.
Establish and maintain project scope, budget, schedule, staffing plan, deliverables, and client expectations.
Prepare project work plans and coordinate engineering, surveying, permitting, bidding, and construction activities.
Monitor project financial performance, including labor budgets, percent complete, forecast-to-complete, billing, collections, and scope changes.
Identify out-of-scope services and prepare timely additional-service requests.
Coordinate subconsultants, utility companies, review agencies, contractors, and other project stakeholders.
Conduct project kickoff, design-review, progress, client, and construction meetings.
Maintain complete and professional project documentation.
Take ownership of project outcomes rather than simply completing assigned technical tasks.

Client Service

Serve as a responsive and trusted point of contact for assigned municipal and private-sector clients.
Communicate technical issues in a practical and understandable manner.
Provide clear recommendations, identify alternatives, and help clients make informed decisions.
Develop familiarity with each client’s standards, priorities, capital plans, approval processes, and communication preferences.
Participate in public meetings, municipal meetings, development reviews, and client presentations as appropriate.
Build relationships that support client retention, repeat assignments, and responsible business growth.
Notify clients promptly when project scope, schedule, cost, risk, or available information changes.

Quality Assurance and Professional Responsibility

Perform detailed interdisciplinary and technical reviews.
Confirm that project documents are complete, coordinated, constructible, and suitable for their intended purpose.
Ensure that work bearing the engineer’s seal was completed under their responsible charge.
Maintain professional independence and sound judgment concerning public health, safety, and welfare.
Participate in formal project reviews at appropriate design milestones.
Document significant design decisions, assumptions, calculations, and review comments.
Help establish a consistent culture of quality without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Construction and Implementation Support

Support bidding, contractor questions, bid evaluations, and recommendations for award.
Review submittals, shop drawings, requests for information, proposed substitutions, and change-order documentation.
Attend construction meetings and perform site observations when appropriate.
Coordinate with construction inspectors, survey crews, contractors, municipal staff, and utility representatives.
Assist with interpretation of plans and specifications.
Review record information, closeout documents, and final project certifications.
Resolve construction issues in a timely manner while protecting the client and maintaining professional standards.

Staff Development

Mentor engineers, designers, and technical staff.

Review work in a manner that teaches and develops others rather than simply correcting the final product.
Help staff understand the engineering reasoning behind design decisions.
Support professional-development plans, licensure, training, and increased project responsibility.
Contribute to a respectful, accountable, collaborative, and solutions-oriented workplace.

Proposals and Business Development

Assist with project scoping, fee development, staffing plans, and proposal preparation.
Participate in client interviews, presentations, and relationship-development activities.
Identify opportunities to provide additional services to existing clients.

Bachelor of Science degree in Civil Engineering from an accredited program.
Active Professional Engineer license in Michigan, or an active PE license in another state with the demonstrated ability to obtain Michigan licensure promptly through comity.
At least five years of progressively responsible civil engineering experience.
Experience preparing and reviewing civil engineering plans, calculations, reports, specifications, and cost estimates.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Project-management experience involving scope, schedule, budget, staffing, billing, and client communication.

Jacobs' Data Center & Hyperscale practice is experiencing record growth — and civil engineering is at the center of it. Provide civil technical leadership for underground fuel storage systems (UST) supporting large generator plants secondary containment design, leak detection integration, spill containment grading, and EPA and state UST regulatory compliance.
Coordinate geotechnical investigation programs with subconsultants; interpret boring logs and laboratory test data; translate geotechnical findings into earthwork specifications, compaction criteria, and foundation coordination inputs for the structural engineering team.

Permitting, Entitlements & Regulatory Strategy

Lead land use entitlement strategy for greenfield and adaptive-reuse hyperscale campus sites — rezoning applications, conditional use permits, site plan approvals, and variance requests — working closely with owners, land use counsel, and local planning authorities to protect schedule and maximize development yield.
Direct NPDES Construction General Permit compliance strategy for large disturbed-area programs, including SWPPP development, BMP selection, QSP coordination, inspection program design, and regulatory agency response. Lead Clean Water Act Section 404 and Section 401 permitting for sites with jurisdictional wetlands, waterways, or Waters of the U.S. — including wetland delineation coordination, permit application strategy, mitigation planning, and agency negotiation to protect program schedule.

Develop early-release civil permit packages — rough grading permits, land disturbance permits, and utility installation permits — sequenced to support fast-track Design-Build and EPCM construction schedules while full entitlement packages are advanced in parallel.
Serve as the civil SME interface with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ), state regulatory agencies, utility providers, and local planning bodies throughout design, permitting, and construction administration phases.
